messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Weird WAIC value
parts:
Dear nimble developers,

I have an example that the WAIC result is weird in that its WAIC is negative. The reproducible .R file and data (response.txt) are attached.
nimbleList object of type waicList
Field "WAIC":
[1] -37302.21
Field "lppd":
[1] 20938.91
Field "pWAIC":
[1] 2287.81

The data are distributed as beta distribution. It seems the calculation of lppd is not correct, but I don't see why. Hope you could give me some direction about this problem. Thanks a lot in advance.

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Weird WAIC value
parts:
hi Keith,

It's not clear to me that anything is wrong here. The density of a beta distribution is often greater than one (since it has to integrate to 1 over (0,1), which means log-density is bigger than 0, hence lppd can be positive when summing over many observations, and WAIC can be negative.

-Chris

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Weird WAIC value
parts:
Hi Keith, I think the following is probably the best path forward.

Instead of assigning dnorm to the transformed observations, create a user-defined distribution that calculates the density of the original observations. This is akin to using a lognormal distribution on a set of observations rather than a normal distribution on log-transformed observations.  The Jacobian  based on your transformation will be calculated in the user-defined distribution and combined with the dnorm density (which is akin to how one would derive the lognormal distribution as well).

Then the WAIC comparison should just work, since you can just get it from nimble under the beta model and under this other model.

-chris
